pages.text: Mom laid a long teal scarf on the dining-car table. "Passengers today. A conductor wears a scarf to collect tickets. Try it yourself?" Autumn mountains passed outside. Bami stamped eagerly. "Me! I'll do it!"
Bami held one end in their beak and swung it around their neck. One end trailed on the floor; the other dangled over their head! "It won't work!" Bami struggled inside it.
Free of the scarf at last, Bami's eyes filled with tears. "I can't even put on a scarf..." Doing it alone had seemed so exciting, but failing hurt.
Mom spread it on the table. "Not a scarf—a railway! A train goes once around your neck." She tapped its middle. "The starting station." Bami leaned closer. "Once around?"

Pipi called a station, and the train stopped in the mountains. Three sheep sisters wearing matching hats boarded. Mom sang, "One turn of the scarf—a train around your neck!" The sisters joined in. Suddenly it was a game.
First, the starting station! Bami held the middle in their beak and laid it behind their neck. Both ends hung forward together. "Departure!" Bami smiled. Just a railway, nothing scary.
Now once around! Holding one end in their beak, Bami turned their neck and wrapped the scarf once. Mom and the three sisters called, "One turn of the scarf!" Bami stamped happily.
Last, the knot! Bami held one end in a foot and pulled the other beneath it with their beak. Scarf on, all alone! Wings wide, teal scarf fluttering, Bami called, "I did it!"
Now Bami knew the steps. "One, middle behind my neck! Two, once around! Three, tuck the end into a knot!" Scarf on, Bami asked the sisters for tickets. They handed over three, laughing.
Mom cuddled Bami and nuzzled their cheek with her beak. "A conductor who puts on a scarf alone!" A scarf was a railway going once around the neck. One turn of the scarf!
